sell: Before sale: disclose defaults and collect evidence; reduced buyer pool/price possible.
extend: Do not grant extra term without credit/guaranty and cure protections.
hold: Cash flow interrupted; enforce remedies, reserve and re-tenant plan needed.
mitigation: Review rent ledger, notices, guaranties, security, insurance and remedies with counsel; quantify recovery time from actual documents.

sell: Short remaining term can reduce buyer pool; market before notice deadlines only after pricing evidence.
extend: An extension depends on tenant consent and viable store economics; extension alone does not create credit support.
hold: Vacancy, downtime, carrying expense, demolition/reuse and leasing capital could overwhelm rent advantage.
mitigation: Maintain dual-track renewal and alternative-tenant plans; get independent leasing and zoning opinions.

event: Rent reset is below expectation or fixed below market
sell: A buyer prices actual contractual cash flow, not a hoped-for reset.
extend: Could lock in weak rent for years; insist on transparent mechanism, evidence and deadlines.
hold: Renewal economics may not justify keeping the asset.
mitigation: Read the executed option clause; do not assume market rent or tenant renewal. Use independent valuation.

event: Franchisee financial distress or guarantor failure
sell: Credit diligence and disclosure affect buyer price and representations.
extend: Avoid relying on brand name where obligor is a franchisee; seek enforceable credit enhancement.
hold: Concentrated income risk may cause sudden vacancy and legal expense.
mitigation: Verify entity/guarantor from lease, obtain confidential financials, track payment/default notices; avoid publishing identities.

sell: Price may vary with buyer financing and prevailing yield requirements.
extend: Longer lease term can help marketability but cannot guarantee a particular cap rate.
hold: Future terminal value is uncertain; avoid underwriting cap-rate compression as certain.
mitigation: Use independent as-is valuation and stress broad cap-rate/yield ranges; update at decision dates.

event: High property insurance premium, exclusions, or unavailable coverage
sell: Current insurer terms and disclosures matter; uninsurable hazards can impair saleability.
extend: Longer term may leave owner exposed to rising/unavailable coverage unless lease clearly allocates obligations.
hold: Premiums, deductibles and exclusions can erode NNN cash flow and create unfunded catastrophe exposure.
mitigation: Obtain written, comparable commercial quotes; review exclusions, limits, deductibles and rent-loss terms with broker.

event: Property tax reassessment / transfer tax / tax-law change
sell: Closing costs and tax threshold applicability depend on jurisdiction, value, structure and law at closing.
extend: Ownership generally continues; changes to law/assessment may still affect economics.
hold: Assessment changes, new construction or ownership changes may affect taxes; do not assume a fixed effective tax bill.
mitigation: Confirm parcel jurisdiction and assessed value; have tax counsel model scenarios and re-check official rules at transaction date.

event: Deferred maintenance, hidden environmental issue, or code action
sell: May create price adjustment, disclosure, escrow and liability exposure.
extend: Capital spending and lease responsibility may fall on landlord despite NNN label.
hold: Unbudgeted work consumes cash and can disrupt rent or insurability.
mitigation: Commission property condition and environmental diligence; reconcile leases, permits and inspection findings.

sell: Known exposure, insurance and damage can affect marketability and timing; sale is not an instant hedge after event.
extend: Tenant closure and insurance/repair costs can coincide with weaker regional demand.
hold: Physical loss, smoke, evacuation, business interruption and insurance-market withdrawal can compound.
mitigation: Use parcel-level current CAL FIRE/local maps, insurer review, defensible-space/roof assessment and business interruption planning.

event: Major earthquake, surface rupture, liquefaction or landslide
sell: Buyer diligence and post-event market disruption can impair exit; disclose known material conditions.
extend: A long extension could be exposed to major uninsured or underinsured loss.
hold: Structural damage, site access loss, repair costs and rent interruption can coincide with broad market shock.
mitigation: Check CGS official zones and obtain structural/geotechnical review; confirm earthquake coverage, deductible and exclusions.

sell: Mapped zones and flood history can affect buyer/lender diligence.
extend: Unmapped or changing conditions still require drainage/engineering review.
hold: Flood damage, access loss, cleanup and business interruption can recur even outside regulatory mapped high-risk zones.
mitigation: Review FEMA current and preliminary data, local drainage records and site grading; obtain engineering/insurance advice.

event: Regional recession / major employment or demand shock
sell: A sale during shock may realize a lower price; proceeds can then be reinvested at changed yields.
extend: Tenant sales and credit could deteriorate at the same time buyer values fall.
hold: Local demand, rent collection and property value can decline together; diversification limits this concentration but has costs.
mitigation: Stress severe vacancy, rent collection, expenses and exit values; do not treat metro aggregates as site demand forecasts.

event: Local civil disruption / infrastructure interruption / access closure
sell: A temporary disruption can complicate marketing and transaction timing.
extend: Access disruption can impair store revenue and rent collection.
hold: Tenant operations and customer access may be interrupted; NNN expense pass-through may not cover revenue loss.
mitigation: Map site access and critical dependencies after location is privately verified; review business interruption clauses and local hazard plans.

event: Tax-deferred exchange fails or replacement investment underperforms
sell: A 1031 attempt can introduce deadline, boot, financing, concentration, fees and replacement asset risks; tax deferral is not tax elimination.
extend: Retaining the asset avoids exchange execution but leaves concentration and liquidity exposure.
hold: No exchange execution risk, but proceeds remain locked in one asset.
mitigation: Model taxable sale and exchange separately with tax counsel/QI; only compare after-tax cash flows and replacement diligence.

event: Owner-specific liquidity, health, estate, or concentration shock
sell: Liquidity/diversification may help if needed, but transaction costs and taxes may be material.
extend: May increase illiquidity and lock-in; only if consistent with privately set objectives.
hold: Concentrated, illiquid asset may be unsuitable if cash needs or risk capacity change.
mitigation: Use a private fiduciary planning process; do not enter personal financial/health details into public website or public chat.
